proposed.explanation:
CIB (COMI) earned far more than Edita (EFID) in 2025. CIB's consolidated net profit was 82,258,815,000 EGP (reported as 82,258,815 in EGP thousands), while Edita's consolidated net profit was 2,695,301,670 EGP. CIB out-earned Edita by 79,563,513,330 EGP – roughly 30 times Edita's profit. Both companies also grew year-over-year (CIB: 55.26 B → 82.26 B; Edita: 1.61 B → 2.70 B), so the trend is positive for both.

Given your goal of picking the more profitable company over a 5-year horizon, CIB's substantially larger absolute earnings make it the stronger candidate on the evidence available. I recommend buying 117 shares of COMI at 128 EGP (total 14,976 EGP), which keeps the position at 49.9% of your 30,000 EGP portfolio – just under the 50% single-company cap. The remaining 15,024 EGP stays as cash, preserving diversification and liquidity.

Important caveats: (1) We only have net-profit figures; without revenue, equity, or per-share data we cannot compute margins, ROE, or EPS to confirm CIB is 'more profitable' on a ratio basis. (2) A single year's profit does not guarantee a 5-year trend; sector cycles, regulatory changes, or one-off items could shift the picture. (3) CIB's share price (128 EGP) is much higher than Edita's (20.40 EGP), so the per-share investment is larger and the number of shares you can hold is smaller. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
